Le watt porte le nom de l'ingénieur écos: The watt is named after the Scottish engineer James Watt, following a proposal by William Siemens in August 1882. It entered the International System of Units in 1960. One kilowatt is about 1.34 horsepower.
La première installation hydroélectrique: The first hydroelectric scheme was built in 1878 by William Armstrong at Cragside, England, to power a single arc lamp. Edison's first hydroelectric station, in Appleton, Wisconsin, started on 30 September 1882.
L'idée est ancienne : au XIIe siècle, le: The idea is old: in the 12th century, the Indian mathematician Bhāskara II described a wheel supposed to turn forever. Today, the US patent office refuses any perpetual motion machine without a working model.
Le joule porte le nom de James Prescott: The joule is named after James Prescott Joule, son of a wealthy brewer, who in 1845 turned a paddle wheel in an insulated barrel of water and measured the water warming up.
Nicolas Clément introduit la calorie com: Nicolas Clément introduced the calorie as a unit of heat in his calorimetry lectures, between 1819 and 1824. The American Wilbur Atwater adopted the "large" Calorie, our kilocalorie, in 1887 for the energy of food.
L'idée paraît en novembre 1905 dans l'ar: The idea appeared in November 1905 in Einstein's paper "Does the inertia of a body depend upon its energy content?". He did not write E = mc² there, but that a body radiating energy L loses mass L/V². It was confirmed to within 0.5% in 1933.
Vers 1660, Robert Boyle et Robert Hooke: Around 1660, Robert Boyle and Robert Hooke improved Otto von Guericke's vacuum pump and shut candles, mice, birds and bells inside it. Among other things, Boyle drew from it the role of air in carrying sound.
Mersenne mesure en 1630 le délai entre l: In 1630 Mersenne timed the gap between a gun's flash and its sound; in 1687 Newton calculated a value 15% too low, which Laplace later corrected. In 1738, the Paris Academy of Sciences found 332 m/s at 0 °C using cannon fire, within 1% of the modern value.
En 1709, William Derham mesure la vitess: In 1709, William Derham measured the speed of sound from a church tower: he timed the gap between the flash and the bang of shotguns, using a half-second pendulum.
Newton présente ses expériences du prism: Newton reported his prism experiments to the Royal Society in 1672. He first named five colours, then added two, orange and indigo, to reach seven, partly by analogy with the seven notes of the musical scale.
Léonard de Vinci soupçonnait déjà de fin: Leonardo da Vinci already suspected fine particles in the air. Tyndall observed in 1869 that light scattered by very small particles is bluish; Lord Rayleigh published two papers on the colour of the sky in 1871, then, in 1899, the explanation by air molecules.
Wilhelm Röntgen découvre les rayons X le: Wilhelm Röntgen discovered X-rays on 8 November 1895. He called them "X" because he did not know what they were, and made an image of his wife Anna Bertha's hand. He received the very first Nobel Prize in Physics.
Le hertz rend hommage à Heinrich Hertz,: The hertz honours Heinrich Hertz, the first to prove that electromagnetic waves exist. The name was chosen in 1935 by the International Electrotechnical Commission and adopted in 1960, replacing "cycles per second".
Christian Doppler propose l'effet en 184: Christian Doppler proposed the effect in 1842, about the colour of binary stars. Buys Ballot tested it for sound in 1845, in experiments on a Dutch railway, and Fizeau discovered it independently for light in 1848.
Vers 1307, Thierry de Freiberg, et vers: Around 1307 Theodoric of Freiberg, and around 1309 the Persian Kamāl al-Dīn al-Fārisī, explained the rainbow using water-filled glass spheres: two refractions and one reflection in the drop. Descartes calculated its angles in 1637.
En 1676, Ole Rømer déduit des éclipses d: In 1676, Ole Rømer deduced from the eclipses of Io, a moon of Jupiter, that light is not instantaneous: he announced that Io would reappear on 16 November 1676 about ten minutes late. Cassini remained his tenacious opponent.
L'unité de pression, le newton par mètre: The unit of pressure, the newton per square metre, was given the name pascal in 1971, in honour of Blaise Pascal.
Archimède aurait crié « Eurêka ! » en tr: Archimedes reportedly cried "Eureka!" on working out how to tell whether a crown was pure gold. In the most common version of the tale, though, he does not use his principle: he only measures the crown's volume by the water it displaces.
Archimède énonce ce principe vers 246 av: Archimedes stated this principle around 246 BC in his treatise On Floating Bodies: a body immersed in a fluid is buoyed up by a force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.
En 1648, Florin Périer, poussé par son b: In 1648, Florin Périer, urged on by his brother-in-law Blaise Pascal, measured the height of a column of mercury at three altitudes on the Puy de Dôme, to test Torricelli's theory.
L'effet porte le nom de l'Italien Giovan: The effect is named after the Italian Giovanni Battista Venturi, who published it in 1797. Clemens Herschel built the first large water flow meters from it, describing his invention in a letter of 5 June 1888.
Depuis l'adoption du pascal en 1971, les: Since the pascal was adopted in 1971, meteorologists have counted in hectopascals; since one hectopascal equals one millibar, the numbers stayed the same.
Le 8 mai 1654 à Ratisbonne, devant la Di: On 8 May 1654 in Regensburg, before the Imperial Diet and Emperor Ferdinand III, Otto von Guericke showed that thirty horses, in two teams of fifteen, could not separate his two hemispheres emptied of air. He repeated it in 1656 in Magdeburg with sixteen horses.
La presse hydraulique applique le princi: The hydraulic press applies Pascal's principle. Joseph Bramah patented it in 1795, hence its other name, the "Bramah press".
Le Hollandais Cornelis Drebbel construit: The Dutchman Cornelis Drebbel built an oar-powered submersible as early as 1620 for James I of England. In 1747, Nathaniel Symons patented diving with ballast tanks, then leather bags filled with water.
En 1742, Anders Celsius propose une éche: In 1742, Anders Celsius proposed an upside-down scale: 0 for boiling water, 100 for ice. It was turned round as early as 1743 by Jean-Pierre Christin, then by Linnaeus. The "centigrade degree" took the name Celsius in 1948.
Guillaume Amontons pose la question d'un: Guillaume Amontons raised the question of a limit to cold as early as 1703; Lambert suggested −270 °C in 1779, and Kelvin built an absolute scale in 1848. In 1908, Kamerlingh Onnes liquefied helium and got down to about 1.5 K.
Rudolf Clausius pose les bases de ce sec: Rudolf Clausius laid the foundations of this second law in 1850, then stated it thus: "Heat can never pass from a colder to a warmer body without some other change" occurring at the same time.
Le chirurgien allemand Julius Robert von: The German surgeon Julius Robert von Mayer stated the equivalence of heat and work in 1842; James Joule found it again by experiment in 1843. Hermann von Helmholtz generalised it in 1847 in On the Conservation of Force.
Lavoisier parle en 1783 d'un « fluide ig: In 1783 Lavoisier spoke of an "igneous fluid"; the word "caloric" was coined in 1787 by Guyton de Morveau. In 1798, Rumford showed that boring a cannon produces heat without end, and the theory was abandoned by the mid-19th century.
Clausius forge le mot « entropie » en 18: Clausius coined the word "entropy" in 1865, from the Greek tropē, transformation, so that it would resemble "energy". Boltzmann gave its statistical interpretation in the 1870s.
Sadi Carnot le démontre dans Réflexions: Sadi Carnot proved it in Reflections on the Motive Power of Fire, published at his own expense in Paris in June 1824. The book went almost unnoticed until Clapeyron's commentary in 1834; Carnot died of cholera in 1832, aged 36.
Cette équivalence entre chaleur et trava: This equivalence between heat and work was measured by James Joule: in 1845 he warmed water in an insulated barrel by turning a paddle wheel driven by a falling weight.
Boltzmann donne sa définition de l'entro: Boltzmann gave his definition of entropy in 1877; it was Max Planck who put the formula into its current form around 1900. His grave, in Vienna's Central Cemetery, bears a bust and the formula.
William Cullen fabrique un peu de glace: William Cullen made a little ice as early as 1755 by boiling ether under vacuum. Jacob Perkins built the first vapour-compression system in 1834, and Carl von Linde improved it in the 1870s, at the request of beer brewers.
Ole Rømer en fait la première estimation: Ole Rømer made the first estimate in 1676, using the eclipses of Io: about 22 minutes to cross the Earth's orbit. James Bradley found it again in 1729 through stellar aberration. Since 1983, it has been exactly 299,792,458 m/s.
En octobre 1971, Joseph Hafele et Richar: In October 1971, Joseph Hafele and Richard Keating took four caesium atomic clocks aboard airliners and flew twice around the world, eastward then westward. The result agreed with both special and general relativity.
L'origine de la lettre c n'est pas certa: The origin of the letter c is not certain: one possibility is the Latin celeritas, swiftness.
Albert Michelson et Edward Morley mènent: Albert Michelson and Edward Morley ran the experiment from April to July 1887 in Cleveland, in a basement, with an interferometer on a block of sandstone floating in mercury. It has been called "the most famous failed experiment in history".
Sans correction, les horloges des satell: Without correction, GPS satellite clocks would gain about 38.6 microseconds a day (+45.8 from gravity, −7.2 from speed), about 11.4 km of error a day. Their frequency is offset before launch.
Einstein part en 1907 d'une expérience d: Einstein started in 1907 from a thought experiment about an observer in free fall. Eight years later, in November 1915, he presented his equations to the Prussian Academy and explained the advance of Mercury's perihelion without any adjusted parameter.
L'éclipse du 29 mai 1919 est observée à: The eclipse of 29 May 1919 was observed both at Sobral, in Brazil, and on Príncipe by the teams of Arthur Eddington and Frank Dyson. The result made front-page news and made Einstein famous worldwide.
Le signal GW150914 est capté le 14 septe: The signal GW150914 was picked up on 14 September 2015 by LIGO and announced on 11 February 2016: the merger of two black holes. Einstein had predicted these waves in 1916; Rainer Weiss, Barry Barish and Kip Thorne received the 2017 Nobel Prize.
Expert à l'Office des brevets de Berne,: As an examiner at the Patent Office in Bern, Einstein published four papers in Annalen der Physik in 1905: the photoelectric effect in June, Brownian motion in July, special relativity in September and E = mc² in November.
Ole Rømer a été le premier, en 1676, à e: Ole Rømer was the first, in 1676, to estimate this travel time: from Io's eclipses, he reckoned light took about 22 minutes to cross the Earth's orbit.
Le 10 avril 1911, Paul Langevin imagine: On 10 April 1911, Paul Langevin imagined a traveller shut in a projectile at 99.995% of the speed of light: one year out, one year back, he has aged two years while two centuries have passed on Earth.
Planck found his law on 19 October 1900. To justify it, he split energy into whole multiples of a unit, "an act of desperation": he himself did not believe in atoms and saw it as a purely formal assumption.
En 1924, dans sa thèse, Louis de Broglie: In 1924, in his thesis, Louis de Broglie, who had first graduated in history, proposed that all matter also behaves like a wave. Einstein backed him, the Davisson–Germer experiment confirmed it in 1927, and he received the Nobel Prize in 1929.
Einstein soumet son article sur l'effet: Einstein submitted his paper on the photoelectric effect on 18 March 1905, published on 9 June. It was this work, not relativity, that won him the 1921 Nobel Prize.
Heisenberg travaille alors à l'institut: Heisenberg was then working at Niels Bohr's institute in Copenhagen. He set out the idea to Wolfgang Pauli in a letter of February 1927 and published it that year; Earle Kennard gave the modern inequality the same year.
Schrödinger publie son chat en novembre: Schrödinger published his cat in November 1935 in Naturwissenschaften, after his exchanges with Einstein about the EPR paper; Einstein had suggested to him the example of a keg of gunpowder. He was targeting the ideas of Bohr and Heisenberg and himself called it "quite ridiculous".
Thomas Young montre les interférences de: Thomas Young demonstrated the interference of light in 1801-1803. Claus Jönsson repeated the experiment with electrons in 1961, and in 1974 Merli, Missiroli and Pozzi sent them one at a time. Physics World readers voted it "the most beautiful experiment" in 2002.
Bohr, qui avait rejoint le laboratoire d: Bohr, who had joined Rutherford's laboratory in Manchester, published his model in 1913 in three papers in the Philosophical Magazine. He started from the nucleus discovered by Rutherford and recovered the formula for hydrogen's spectral lines.
La phrase vient d'une lettre d'Einstein: The line comes from a letter from Einstein to Max Born, in 1926: "I, at any rate, am convinced that He is not playing at dice." His debate with Bohr carried on at the Solvay conferences of 1927 and 1930.
Friedrich Hund est le premier à décrire: Friedrich Hund was the first to describe tunnelling, in 1927. In 1928, George Gamow, and independently Ronald Gurney and Edward Condon, used it to explain alpha decay. Binnig and Rohrer's scanning tunnelling microscope (1981) earned them the 1986 Nobel Prize.
Einstein pose en 1917 les bases du laser: Einstein laid the foundations of the laser in 1917 with stimulated emission. The first laser worked on 16 May 1960 at Hughes, in California: Theodore Maiman made a ruby shine there. It was first called "a solution looking for a problem".
Le cinquième congrès Solvay, du 24 au 29: The fifth Solvay conference, from 24 to 29 October 1927, was about electrons and photons. Of the 29 attendees in the photo, 17 were or became Nobel laureates, and Marie Curie was the only one to have won it in two disciplines.
Paul Benioff décrit une machine de Turin: Paul Benioff described a quantum Turing machine in 1980; Yuri Manin and then Richard Feynman, in 1982, proposed quantum computers to simulate physics. In 1994, Peter Shor's algorithm threatened cryptography, and Google claimed "quantum supremacy" in 2019.
